title: Prompt about unauthorized Thunderbolt devices
head: 2ae0d797ecf4
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: All three new user units are omitted from the omarchy-settings package recipe
leads.consequence: The recipe copies default/ to /usr/share/omarchy/default/ but explicitly installs only selected units to /usr/lib/systemd/user. On packaged first run the single systemctl --user enable --now call includes three nonexistent units and aborts the leaf under set -e, potentially preventing unrelated Bluetooth, sleep, fcitx5, crash and migration notification units from being enabled. Existing-user migration suppresses enable failures, creates dangling symlinks, reports start errors without failing and omarchy-migrate:93-96 marks it complete; fixing packaging later does not retry migration automatically. Explicitly install all three units to /usr/lib/systemd/user before enabling them.

leads.summary: Persistent notification IDs suppress the next login and fast unplug/replug
leads.consequence: The notified ID stays on disk when the same unauthorized accessory is still present after a reboot, so a dismissed or missed actionable toast never reappears on later logins. The same happens if it disconnects and reconnects between the periodic scans (the comparison only sees the current set). The run fixture sends exactly one toast, then sends none on the next invocation with the same HOME, and none on an unplug/replug between scans. Scope the state to a login or connection generation, or ensure state is cleared on disconnect through an actual event source.
leads.triage: already_in_opus (reboot persistence = F2 residual); fast unplug/replug between scans facet dropped as low value

leads.summary: Open #11874 introduces a competing Thunderbolt approval workflow and same-line first-run conflict
leads.consequence: #11874 (diverged, not stacked) adds its own graphical Thunderbolt watcher, notification and protected approval helper for the same pending accessory. It disables Bolt auto-enrollment but explicitly allows per-device authorization. With both units enabled and packaging fixed, the user gets competing clickable prompts; clicking this PR's 'Authorize for this session' calls Bolt directly, bypassing #11874's identity/review/request protocol and root trust policy, and its 'enroll' path can fail while AuthMode is disabled. Merge-file of the first-run lists yields conflict markers at their respective appended lines, so a naive one-sided resolution also drops one feature's units. Coordinate one approval path or gate this notifier when #11874 is enabled.
leads.triage: already_in_opus (N3 info); bolt AuthMode/protocol-bypass details not published (depend on #11874 merging)

leads.summary: Timer and watcher conditions are only tested when they start, not reevaluated as hardware and opt-out change
leads.consequence: If the domain glob is absent when timers.target starts, systemd skips the timer and will not later start it when a Thunderbolt controller appears; sysfs directory event is not a reliable replacement. If the opt-out file exists when graphical-session.target starts, both timer and path remain skipped after it is removed until a subsequent explicit start/login. Conversely, creating the opt-out file after the timer has started does not stop the active timer: it still schedules service starts (which the service then skips) every 30 seconds, contrary to the comment promising the timer goes quiet. Use active lifecycle management or a condition on the triggered service with appropriate timer stop/restart logic.

leads.summary: The package-default test fixture omits three new explicit installation assertions
leads.consequence: package_defaults checks every listed package-owned unit against the external PKGBUILD at lines 168-174. The new service, path and timer have no rows here, so the test can still pass while H1 strands the feature on packaged systems. Add three rows mapping default/systemd/user/omarchy-thunderbolt-notify.{service,path,timer} to /usr/lib/systemd/user/omarchy-thunderbolt-notify.{service,path,timer}.

leads.summary: An existing but empty device_name leaves an unnamed prompt rather than the UUID fallback
leads.consequence: The new fallback is selected only when the sysfs attribute is absent/unreadable, not when it exists with a zero-length name. Both scripts then use the empty string in the toast, gum label, and authorization header. Linux DROM name parsing can allocate an empty name from a zero-length name entry and exposes the attribute whenever the allocated name pointer exists. A command-only fixture with an empty device_name generated a toast beginning ' connected' (no name). Check -n on the read value and fall back to unique_id for empty names too.

leads.summary: The submitted 'full regression suite' is not discoverable or self-contained
leads.consequence: No test under test/shell.d covers either new script or unit. ./test/all invokes only test/cli and test/shell; shell globs test/shell.d/*-test.sh, so root-level run_suite.sh is never run. If invoked independently, it hardcodes /opt/data/dev/omarchy-pr12510 and /tmp/tbtest/fakebin without creating them and writes/deletes fixed /tmp/tbtest paths, so it cannot validate the checked-out source reliably. Move the cases into a self-contained test/shell.d/thunderbolt-test.sh using mktemp and stubs under a private directory; assert actual argv and success/failure as well as emitted toast.

leads.summary: Open #10582's first-run fix conflicts with the new appended units
leads.consequence: #10582 (diverged) replaces this PR's multi-unit enable call with an array and single-unit loop. A three-way merge at the pinned base yields conflict markers around this PR's three names versus #10582's array. If #10582's side wins without explicitly appending all three names inside units=(...), the Thunderbolt units never start on fresh installs even after packaging is repaired; if this PR's side wins it regresses #10582's missing-unit isolation. Resolve by retaining its per-unit enable loop and adding service, path and timer to the array.
leads.triage: factual -> coordinator verified (gh pr view/diff #10582; Opus later merge-tree)

leads.summary: The path-unit comment still implies a possible instant sysfs create trigger without a kernel event source
leads.consequence: systemd PathChanged uses inotify IN_CREATE etc. on the watched directory, but kernfs's device-directory insertion links/activates nodes and updates timestamps without emitting fsnotify for the new child; IN_MODIFY is absent from PathChanged as well. On these kernel sources a hotplug cannot make the path unit deliver an instant scan, so the 30-second timer is the hotplug mechanism, not merely a backstop. Remove or qualify the claim that this path may shorten latency, or use a udev event source. This is a dependency premise check, not hardware validation.

leads.summary: A device_name beginning with a gum flag aborts the menu after authorization
leads.consequence: Thunderbolt DROM device_name is device-controlled text, not a validated command operand. A name beginning '--help' is parsed by gum style as a flag: the first label shows gum's help instead of the name. After the user authorizes, gum style --foreground 2 with a name beginning --help returns 80 (unknown flag) under set -e, so the script stops before removing the notified ID and before sending the success toast, although sysfs authorized has become 1. A command-only run with the real gum binary and a stub boltctl confirmed exit 80, authorized=1 and the state entry retained. Pass '--' before every device-controlled style text argument (or use stdin).
leads.triage: behavioural -> Opus follow-up Q2 confirmed with real gum

limits: No real Thunderbolt hardware or live user systemd/bolt/notification session was available. Behavioural receipts use isolated synthetic sysfs stubs under review.py. H9 is grounded in upstream source, not a live hardware run.
GitHub related-PR results and package recipe were inspected read-only; no branches were fetched into the shared repository and no public comments or reviews of #12510 were read.

flags.claim: The `thunderbolt` module is in the initramfs, so no sysfs path separates "no controller" from "controller powered down".
flags.why: Two lost qualifiers. (1) The module is in the initramfs only on x86_64: omarchy-settings removes etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d on aarch64 (omarchy-settings PKGBUILD:218-223). (2) 'no sysfs path' goes beyond the evidence. I only showed that /sys/bus/thunderbolt exists either way. Platform-specific paths exist on some machines, e.g. the Intel WMI force_power device (kernel thunderbolt.rst:437-445, drivers/platform/x86/intel/wmi/thunderbolt.c). Also dropped: the cost of the suggestion (removing the condition brings back 30 s polling on every x86_64 install, the earlier point).

flags.claim: That also blocks every other waiting device in the same run.
flags.why: The menu loops over waiting devices in sysfs glob order. Devices that sort before the dash-named one are prompted normally before the abort; only those after it are blocked. The run placed the dash device first (0-1 before 0-3).

flags.claim: The patched run handled every case.
flags.why: The patched run covered four tested cases (dash + Dock, --help, empty name, Dock control) plus the direct gum probes. The mutant also contained the empty-name fallback from the next bullet, not just the two `--` changes.

flags.claim: ... would avoid shipping a script nobody else can run.
flags.why: run_suite.sh is not shipped by any package. The omarchy PKGBUILD installs only bin/*, install, migrations, themes, shell and version; omarchy-settings copies config, etc, applications, default and named branding files. It would be committed to the repo, not shipped. Also dropped: to be picked up by ./test/shell it must be named *-test.sh (test/shell:10) and, per AGENTS.md:115, source base-test.sh.

flags.claim: omarchy-migrate runs every pending migration in name order, so an older timestamp has no practical effect.
flags.why: Lost qualifier. It has no practical effect here because this migration does not depend on state set up by a later one. The repo's migration guide says migrations are strictly ordered (agents/skills/migrations.md:129), so as a general statement it is too strong. Supporting fact that was dropped: quattro itself merged the backdated 1788163635 and 1788996284 after this base.

flags.claim: before 2ae0d797: the unconditional timer found it within about 30 s
flags.why: The old timer has OnUnitActiveSec=30s and AccuracySec=5s, so the worst case is about 35 s. The earlier public review said "up to about 35 s". My own report wrote "~30 s", which is the same imprecision.

flags.claim: Sandboxed runs executed the unmodified PR scripts against a synthetic sysfs tree
flags.why: The scripts were copied with exactly one line changed (`devices_dir=` redirected to the synthetic tree; asserted single substitution). Everything else was unmodified.

flags.claim: The repository's `./test/cli` and `./test/shell` suites showed the same results on base and head.
flags.why: Literally true, but it reads as a clean pass. ./test/cli stops at the same environment-dependent vscode theme check on both, so its later checks did not run; I checked the new bins' metadata by hand. ./test/shell fails the same 5 of 252 files on both (environment/fixture gaps).

flags.claim: The units are still not packaged, and at the new base that also stops first-run from completing. (also heading line 25: 'Unpackaged units now also stop first-run from completing')
flags.why: Lost condition. First-run fails only if the PR ships before the omarchy-pkgs change. Line 46 states the condition; the outcome line and heading do not. The mechanism itself is correct.

flags.why: Outside my evidence. Roles, models and efforts are recorded by the coordinator (subagents / pi_job.py verify / check-result).

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** Follow-up on the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12510#issuecomment-5828327051) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12510#issuecomment-5830125700), checked at `2ae0d797`. **Verified:** most of the earlier points are fixed. Two issues remain.
- The units are still not packaged. If the PR ships before that packaging change, at the new base it also stops first-run from completing.
- The new timer condition, which the earlier review suggested, can turn off detection for a whole session on some hardware. That suggestion is corrected below.

| Earlier point | Status at `2ae0d797` |
|---|---|
| `--exec` passed as one string | **Resolved.** The toast is sent with a two-word click command. |
| Pruning never removed the id | **Resolved.** Unplug and replug now notifies again, and a device authorized outside the menu is pruned. |
| Units not packaged | **Still present**, with larger impact (below). |
| Path unit does not fire on connect | **Partly addressed.** The comment no longer promises an instant trigger (see smaller points). |
| Migration started only the service | **Resolved.** The migration starts the timer, path and service. The TTY fallback is idempotent. |
| `authorized=2` reported as failure | **Resolved.** |
| Devices without `device_name` invisible | **Resolved.** They get a toast and a menu entry named by `unique_id`. |
| "Enrolled devices" label | **Resolved.** "Connected devices" matches `boltctl list` output. |
| Timer polls on every install | **Changed.** Machines without Thunderbolt are now quiet, but see the new finding. |
| Rebase conflict / migration timestamp | Conflict **resolved**. The timestamp point is **withdrawn**: `omarchy-migrate` runs every pending migration in name order, and this migration does not depend on a later one, so its older timestamp has no practical effect. |
| Explicit-only stance | **Verified**, still holds. `boltctl` runs only after a menu choice. Esc, Ctrl-C and Skip make no call. |

The author's `run_suite.sh` cannot run as committed. An independent sandboxed harness reproduced the behaviors it claims on the new head, and the old head failed them as expected.

### Without packaging, first-run no longer completes

The three units are still missing from the `omarchy-settings` and `omarchy-settings-dev` PKGBUILDs in omarchy-pkgs and from `package_defaults` in `test/shell.d/config-test.sh`. `docs/file-layout.md` asks for an `install -Dm644` line in the `omarchy-settings` PKGBUILD for this kind of file. An offline `systemctl --root` enable of the exact first-run list produced these results:

| Unit files present | Exit | Links created |
|---|---|---|
| Existing units only, new names in the list | 1 | 0 |
| Existing list without the new names (control) | 0 | 7 |
| New units installed | 0 | 10 |

At the rebased base the failure goes further than the earlier review described:

```text
omarchy-provision-first-run
  └─ enable-user-units.sh (set -euo pipefail)
       systemctl --user enable --now ... <3 missing units>  -> exit 1, nothing enabled
       omarchy-hook-install theme-set ...                   -> skipped
  -> step failed, first-run marker not written
  -> first-run retries at every login, including the welcome and Wi-Fi/update notifications
```

**Impact:** On a new install built without the packaging change, none of the first-run user units are enabled, the theme-set hook is not installed, and first-run repeats at every login. `omarchy-settings-dev` builds from the `quattro` tip, so a dev build right after a merge would be affected unless the omarchy-pkgs change lands with it.

**Suggested change:** Add `install -Dm644` lines for the three units in both PKGBUILDs, and add the three units to `package_defaults`. Open PR #10582 rewrites this same enable call as a per-unit loop, which would contain the failure. If both land, the three new units need to go into its `units=(...)` list.

### New: the timer condition can disable detection for the whole session

The timer now has `ConditionPathExistsGlob=/sys/bus/thunderbolt/devices/domain*`. The earlier review suggested this condition, and it has a gap:

- systemd checks a unit's conditions only when the unit starts (`src/core/unit.c`). A running timer never rechecks them, and a skipped timer is not retried.
- `domainN` exists only while the controller's PCI device is bound (`drivers/thunderbolt/pci.c`, `domain.c`).
- boltctl(1) notes that a controller not in "native enumeration mode" can be completely powered down by the firmware. The kernel's Thunderbolt admin guide says to plug in a device "so that the host controller appears".

```text
login, nothing plugged in, controller powered down
  timer:   domain* absent -> skipped, not retried this session
  path:    no event on connect (kernfs)
  service: one scan at login, nothing found
device plugged in later -> no toast until the timer next starts (normally next login)
before 2ae0d797: the unconditional timer found it within about 30 to 35 s
```

This is based on kernel, systemd and bolt sources and docs only. It was not observed on hardware, and how many machines behave this way was not measured.

**Impact:** On affected machines, a device connected after login gets no prompt for the rest of the session. The path-unit comment says "the 30s backstop timer is what guarantees detection", which does not hold there.

**Suggested change:** Remove the `domain*` condition from the timer and keep the opt-out condition. That brings back the 30 s polling on every x86_64 install, because the `thunderbolt` module is in the x86_64 initramfs and `/sys/bus/thunderbolt` exists whether or not a controller is present. Alternatively, a trigger-only udev rule on Thunderbolt device add events (`TAG+="systemd"` plus `ENV{SYSTEMD_USER_WANTS}`) authorizes nothing and would replace both the path unit and the timer.

### Smaller points

- **Dash-leading device names break the menu.** `device_name` comes from the device's DROM without filtering. `bin/omarchy-thunderbolt` passes it to `gum style` as a positional argument. In a sandboxed run with the real gum 2.0.0:
  - A name like `-x` exits 80 before the prompt. That also blocks any waiting device listed after it in the same run.
  - A name like `--help` prints gum's help instead of the name. After a successful enroll, the success line exits 80 under `set -e`, so the confirmation toast is skipped and the terminal reports failure although the device is authorized.

  Suggested change: `gum style --bold -- "$name"` and `gum style --foreground 2 -- "$name is authorized for this system."`. With those two changes and the empty-name fallback below, the patched run handled every tested case.
- **Empty `device_name`.** The kernel can expose the attribute with an empty value, so the `unique_id` fallback is skipped and the toast and menu show a blank name. The flow still completes. Suggested change for both scripts: `[[ -n ${device_names[$unique_id]} ]] || device_names[$unique_id]=$unique_id`.
- **State outlives the session.** The comment in `bin/omarchy-thunderbolt-check` says "this session", but the state is kept in `~/.local/state`. A device that was toasted, then skipped or dismissed, and that stays connected across logout or reboot is not announced again until it disconnects. Either move the state to `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` or reword the comment.
- **Path unit.** The new comment says `PathChanged` "may fire on some kernels". In Linux v7.2 kernfs, creating a device node emits no fsnotify event, so the unit stays inert. Keeping it is harmless on its own, but the comment could say it does not fire on connect.
- **`run_suite.sh` at the repo root.** It hardcodes an author-local path, writes and deletes under `/tmp/tbtest`, and depends on stubs that are not in the PR. `./test/shell` only runs `test/shell.d/*-test.sh`, so it is never picked up. Moving it into `test/shell.d/` as a `*-test.sh` file with its stubs, or dropping it, would avoid committing a script nobody else can run.
- **Related PR #11874** adds a separate Thunderbolt approval prompt and appends units to the same `enable-user-units.sh` list. If both merge, one device could get two prompts, and the second merge conflicts on that list.
- **Stale text.** The PR description still describes an instant `PathChanged` trigger and "Verifies `authorized == 1`".

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of `2ae0d797` against `quattro` at `c3e67f5d`, with the earlier head `44d34868` as the negative control, current omarchy-pkgs, bolt 0.9.11, systemd v262 and Linux v7.2 sources. Sandboxed runs executed the PR scripts, changed only to point at a synthetic sysfs tree, with the real `omarchy-notification-send` and `boltctl`, `busctl`, `gum` and `systemctl` stubbed. The device-name cases used the real `gum style`, with only `gum choose` stubbed. They also covered the migration, the first-run script and an offline `systemctl --root` enable check (systemd 261.2). The repository's `./test/cli` and `./test/shell` suites showed no new failures: `./test/cli` stops at the same environment-dependent check on base and head, and `./test/shell` fails the same 5 of 252 files on both. No Thunderbolt hardware, live bolt daemon, user systemd session or notification daemon was used. The timer-condition and path-unit points are from source and documentation only. `run_suite.sh` was read, not run.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
